Question: What is the role of the kidneys in the human body? Describe how urine is formed. (5 marks)
My answer: The kidneys are a pair of bean-shaped organs in the abdomen, one on each side of the backbone. Their main job is to remove nitrogenous wastes such as urea from the blood. Each kidney has many tiny filtering units called nephrons. Blood enters a nephron through the glomerulus, where it is filtered under pressure into Bowman's capsule. As the filtrate moves along the tubule, useful substances like glucose, amino acids and most of the water are reabsorbed into the blood. The liquid left behind is urine. It passes through the ureters into the urinary bladder, where it is stored, and is finally passed out through the urethra.

Q. Describe the major causes of poverty in India. (5 marks)
Answer: Poverty in India has many causes. First, during British rule the economy was exploited and traditional industries like handicrafts were destroyed. Second, the population grew very fast, so the benefits of growth were shared by more and more people. Third, economic growth was low for many years and enough jobs were not created. Many farmers have very small pieces of land and depend on the rain. Unequal distribution of land and other resources is another big reason. Many poor families also take loans for social functions and fall into a debt trap.

The Joy of Reading
In today's digital world, students spend most of their free time on mobile phones and social media, and reading books has become a forgotten habit. However, reading is one of the best ways to improve our knowledge, vocabulary and imagination. When we read, we travel to new places and meet new people without leaving our room. Reading also improves concentration, which helps in studies and exams. Schools should set up good libraries and give students a reading period every week. Parents can gift books instead of gadgets. Public libraries should also stay open in the evenings so that students can read after school. Reading a newspaper every morning keeps us aware of what is happening in the country and the world. If we read for even twenty minutes a day, we can become better thinkers and better writers.
